note: Recorded off a running prismd by crates/prismd/tests/ui_show.rs. The sequences, the presets, the executors and every answer are the daemon's own, taken from a fresh client's snapshot. Regenerate with: cargo test -p prismd --test ui_show -- --ignored

steps.what: make a cue list to store into: a fresh show has none at all
put it on an executor, which is what makes it playable
select three PARs
and dial them red
what would storing cue 1 do? it does not exist yet, so this is a create
store it
select two of them again
and dial them green
what would storing cue 1 again do? **this is the overwrite an operator has to be told about**: the three reds are still in the programmer, so they are replaced, and the two greens are added
store it anyway: merge is what the daemon has, and it said so
store a second cue
name it
give it a fade
and a trigger that carries a time with it
renumber it to 1.5, which moves it up the list
a fade that runs backwards: refused, and nothing moves
a renumber onto a number that is taken: refused, and nothing moves
clear the programmer
select the PARs again
dial a blue
and a dimmer value on a PAR's white
what would storing preset 1 in the Colour pool do? a create, and it counts the colour values only
store it, with a name and a scribble-strip colour
clear again
select the PARs
and apply the preset, which is what puts a **link** in the programmer
store a cue out of it: its parts carry the preset reference
clear once more
select the PARs
dial a different blue
what would storing over preset 1 do? an edit of a preset: the three blues are replaced and the three whites are kept
edit the preset — **and cue 3 follows it**, which is the whole claim
a preview of a store into a sequence that is not there: refused, in the daemon's own words
clear the programmer for the last time
and a preview with nothing to store: refused, but it still says what is filed under that number
delete a cue: the numbers left do not close up
delete a cue that is not there: refused, and nothing moves
a sequence number that is taken: refused, and the cue list survives
fire the list
step it again
and stop it
a Go on an executor with nothing on it: refused
and take the last edit back
